title: SD: system suite — test/system/halt-mechanism.test.js fails on clean main (not host-related, cause unknown)
description:
## Problem

`test/system/halt-mechanism.test.js` fails under `npm run test:system`: the workspace-halt system test (LIN-2994/LIN-3044 family). The assertion that a follow-up stays queued while the workspace is halted fails (assertion `follow-up still queued`, `test/system/halt-mechanism.test.js:79`).

## Why it matters

The halt is the operator's stop control. If this is a real defect (a follow-up gets claimed or dropped while halted) the stop does not hold; if it is test-versus-Harbour drift, the suite has no working witness of the halt. Either way the standing red hides the next real break. The system suite is also the only place these behaviours are exercised end to end, and nothing automated watches it.

## Reproduces on

Repo: **JKershaw/simple-dispatcher**. `npm run test:system` (not in CI; `ci.yml` runs only `npm test`), with `HARBOUR_DIR` pointing at a LinearViewer checkout. Measured by LIN-4181 (merged as PR #309, `11a1279`) on the runner host:

* identical on clean `main` (`0992f39`) and on the LIN-4181 head, run from a workspace clone, a checkout in `/private/tmp`, and a checkout with `TMPDIR` inside `state/`;
* identical against Harbour `9e397e6b`, `10b2c82f` and `0dc1620e`;
* each also fails when its file is run on its own.
  So it is **not** host or location noise, **not** Harbour-version skew and **not** a LIN-4181 regression. The cause is **not known**: LIN-4181 triaged it only far enough to rule those out.

## Acceptance

* The cause is found and stated on this ticket: a real Simple Dispatcher defect, a real Harbour defect (then a Harbour ticket exists), or drift between the test and Harbour.
* `test/system/halt-mechanism.test.js` passes against the Harbour checkout it is run with, **or** is skipped with a stated, checked reason. It is not loosened to pass: the assertion on line 79 keeps guarding what it guards.
* `npm run test:system` no longer lists `halt-mechanism` among its failures, run from a workspace clone, with the other three named failures treated separately.

## Anchors

* `test/system/halt-mechanism.test.js:79`
* `test/system/harness/harbour.js` (how Harbour is started), `test/system/README.md`
* Related: LIN-2471 (an earlier, different red case in the same suite), LIN-4181 (found this; the triage is in its review comments and close-out)

## Unvalidated idea

None worth stating: the cause is unknown. A first step is to run this file alone with Harbour's logs kept and look at what the queue/feed holds at the failing assertion.

---

*Priority: priorityLevel 3 (High): it guards the halt/stop control, so a real failure there is a safety defect; likelihood is unknown. Not 4 because no production symptom has been reported and the suite is not in CI. Label: Bug (the workspace catalog has no narrower type label).*

comments.body: Same cause as LIN-4186: LIN-4079 (`bd6d2cf`) made a follow-up to a CANCELLED session a refused (reject) verdict, and this system test still expected it to be held and then resumed. At `bd6d2cf^` this test passes; at `bd6d2cf` it fails. Linked as a duplicate of LIN-4186 and fixed in the same PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/316 (`halt-mechanism.test.js` now asserts the follow-up is refused under the stop and never resumes the cancelled session after the stop clears).
